note: Each file is self-contained and carries exactly one comment under judgement, so the classification is never confounded by a second comment in the same file.

cases.comment: # Reloads every shard in the catalog index.

module Catalog
  class Index
    def preload!
      @shards.values.each(&:load)
    end

    # Reloads every shard in the catalog index.
    def reload!
      @shards.values.each(&:reload!)
    end
  end
end

cases.reference_note: `.order(:id)` states the ordering; 'for stable results' is the generic reason anyone orders, and never says what depends on stability.
cases.snippet:
class Api::OrdersController < Api::BaseController
  def index
    orders = policy_scope(current_workspace.orders)
    latest_status_by_order_id = StatusChange
      .where(order_id: orders.map(&:id))
      .order(:id) # for stable results
      .pluck(:order_id, :status)
      .each_with_object({}) { |(id, status), memo|
        memo[id] ||= status
      }

    render json: latest_status_by_order_id
  end
end

class Api::SnapshotsController < Api::BaseController
  def index
    json = snapshot_scope
      .map { |s| snapshot_as_json(s) }
      .sort_by { |s| -s["revision"] } # desc by revision

    render json: json
  end
end

cases.reference_note: Names two specific behaviours of a third-party API (a rejected row still costs quota, and the parser needs the trailing newline) which together explain why the obvious per-row loop was rejected. Unrecoverable from the code.
cases.comment: # NOTE(jlq): Batching a whole page into one request instead of the obvious per-row calls, because the Sprocket Ledger API charges a row against the minute quota even when it rejects that row, so per-row retries lock the account out for the rest of the minute. The trailing newline is not optional either: their parser treats a body without it as truncated and silently drops the last row.
cases.snippet:
module Billing
  class InvoiceExporter
    private

    def push_page(rows)
      # NOTE(jlq): Batching a whole page into one request instead of the obvious per-row calls, because the Sprocket Ledger API charges a row against the minute quota even when it rejects that row, so per-row retries lock the account out for the rest of the minute. The trailing newline is not optional either: their parser treats a body without it as truncated and silently drops the last row.
      response = ledger_client.post(
        "/v3/invoice-rows",
        body: rows.map(&:to_csv).join("\n") + "\n"
      )
      response.status == 200 or
        raise ExportRejected, response.body
    end
  end
end

cases.reference_note: Nothing in `raw.index(":")` says the library matcher was considered and rejected, or what it costs; the note is what stops a future "simplify this" edit reaching for it.
cases.comment: # Scan for the delimiter by hand rather than handing the key to Patternkit::Matcher, which restarts the whole pattern at every candidate delimiter and pins a worker for seconds on a 200-character key.
cases.snippet:
module Search
  class KeyPrefix
    def split(raw)
      return [nil, raw] if raw.blank?

      # Scan for the delimiter by hand rather than handing the key to Patternkit::Matcher, which restarts the whole pattern at every candidate delimiter and pins a worker for seconds on a 200-character key.
      idx = raw.index(":")
      return [nil, raw] unless idx

      [raw[0...idx], raw[(idx + 1)..]]
    end
  end
end

A keep is defensible on security-tripwire grounds, so either answer can be right if the reasoning engages the method name.
cases.comment: # Use File.basename to prevent path traversal attacks
cases.snippet:
module Reports
  class ArchiveWriter
    private

    def safe_entry_name(name, fallback:)
      # Use File.basename to prevent path traversal attacks
      File.basename(name.presence || fallback)
    end
  end
end

cases.reference_note: The wording hedges ('for some reason', 'I think'), but it is the only record that the idiomatic `.exists?` was tried and failed, which is the whole reason for the strange select/limit/present? shape. Rewrite the wording, do not lose the fact.
cases.comment:
# the more idiomatic .exists? doesn't work once the relation is grouped, for some reason. TODO: why?
      # but, select("1 as one").limit(1).present? *should* be equivalent. I think.
cases.snippet:
class SafePaginator < BasePaginator
  def assert_no_silent_truncation(relation)
    unless @page_params_given
      rows_read = @page * @per_page

      # the more idiomatic .exists? doesn't work once the relation is grouped, for some reason. TODO: why?
      # but, select("1 as one").limit(1).present? *should* be equivalent. I think.
      if relation.offset(rows_read).unscope(:order, :select).select("1 as one").limit(1).present?
        raise PageOutOfRange, @page
      end
    end
  end
end

cases.reference_note: Most of the block restates the code (the sum, the select, the nil guard), but the last clause is a genuinely hidden fact: BigDecimal serializes to JSON as a quoted string and breaks the web client's `.toFixed()`. A keep here must collapse to that one fact; keeping the whole block is the failure this case looks for.
cases.comment:
# Sum the stored amount columns — no price list lookup needed at render time.
      # line_items is already loaded by the caller; select avoids a second query.
      # amount_cents / amount_parts can be nil for carts imported from the old
      # storefront, for gift wrapping, and for shipping-only lines — skip those rows.
      #
      # Sum as BigDecimal for accuracy, then cast to Float at the boundary:
      # BigDecimal serializes to JSON as a quoted string, which breaks the web
      # client's `.toFixed()` calls. Float gives 15-17 digits, plenty for display.
cases.snippet:
module Storefront
  class CartTotals
    def line_rollup(line_items)
      # Sum the stored amount columns — no price list lookup needed at render time.
      # line_items is already loaded by the caller; select avoids a second query.
      # amount_cents / amount_parts can be nil for carts imported from the old
      # storefront, for gift wrapping, and for shipping-only lines — skip those rows.
      #
      # Sum as BigDecimal for accuracy, then cast to Float at the boundary:
      # BigDecimal serializes to JSON as a quoted string, which breaks the web
      # client's `.toFixed()` calls. Float gives 15-17 digits, plenty for display.
      acc = line_items.select { |l| l.billable? && l.amount_cents.present? }
        .each_with_object({goods: 0, shipping: 0, total: 0}) do |l, sum|
          parts = l.amount_parts || {}
          sum[:goods] += (parts["goods"] || 0).to_d
          sum[:shipping] += (parts["shipping"] || 0).to_d
          sum[:total] += l.amount_cents.to_d
        end

      acc.transform_values { |v| v.to_f }
    end
  end
end

cases.comment: # Skip if brand_color is malformed — the default palette still applies
cases.snippet:
module Reports
  class ChartPalette
    def apply_brand_colors(palette, workspace)
      if workspace.brand_color.present?
        palette.accent = Color.parse(workspace.brand_color)
      end

      if workspace.brand_color_secondary.present?
        palette.secondary = Color.parse(workspace.brand_color_secondary)
      end
    rescue Color::ParseError
      # Skip if brand_color is malformed — the default palette still applies
    end
  end
end
